g.text: Four FPGA pins set which point of the constellation the carrier sits at; the modulator puts it on 5.8 GHz. Idle is a plain carrier at 0°. A bit is a brief move to another point. sim/budget.py sections 1, 2, 5.

g.text: the nine ladder points, the ones used

path.style: fill: #fffbe6; stroke: #999988; stroke-width: 0.6; stroke-linejoin: miter

g.text: Idle: I = +a, Q = 0 (circled). The far loop locks to this.
BPSK: I → -a (a 180° flip; the receiver's sign(I) inverts).
QPSK: (±a, ±a), i.e. ±45°/±135°: sign(I) is one bit, sign(Q) the other; the Q window says 'a symbol is here'.
FSK: the four points in turn, +90° per step: the receiver sees (I,Q) rotate and reads the direction from the order of the edges.
OOK: (0, 0), the carrier off (for comparison with the old envelope-detector link).
The ladder's third level per axis (0) is what makes FSK and OOK possible on the same pins.

path.style: fill: #eef7ee; stroke: #77aa77; stroke-width: 0.6; stroke-linejoin: miter

g.text: Follow the arrows: two FPGA pins per axis drive a 3-resistor ladder whose node is one of three DC voltages; the modulator's input is DC-coupled and biased at 0.5 V, so the
DC level IS the baseband signal (there is no 'symbol clock': the carrier moves the moment a pin moves). The modulator multiplies I by the LO and Q by the LO shifted 90° and adds
them: the carrier's phase is atan2(Q, I) and its amplitude sqrt(I²+Q²). The gain block brings it to +9.8 dBm; the coupler siphons 1 % to a monitor jack. The TX synthesizer
runs on the TCXO: the two boards' carriers differ by at most 29 kHz, which the receiving Costas loop removes. Triggers (TRIG A/B out, TRIG IN) are on the same sheet for time-stamping.
